ui.A local workspace for cryptography exper: A local workspace for cryptography experiments and code inspection.
ui.AUTHOR: AUTHOR
ui.Caesar, Vigenère, Atbash, ROT13 and repe: Caesar, Vigenère, Atbash, ROT13 and repeating-key XOR are educational examples, not secure protection. Use AES-GCM or Fernet for real data, and keep keys secret.
ui.Choose a method. Modern encryption uses: Choose a method. Modern encryption uses the optional cryptography package.
ui.Enter text, or Base64 token when decrypt: Enter text, or Base64 token when decrypting…
ui.AES-GCM and Fernet output is a Base64 to: AES-GCM and Fernet output is a Base64 token containing the nonce/metadata and ciphertext. Manage the key in the key panel below; it is validated before every operation. Enigma I is a historical educational simulator, not secure encryption.
ui.Calculate a digest and compare two hash: Calculate a digest and compare two hash strings.
ui.MD5 and SHA-1 are included only for comp: MD5 and SHA-1 are included only for compatibility/testing; do not use them for security-sensitive integrity or passwords.
ui.Derive password hashes using salts and c: Derive password hashes using salts and configurable key-derivation algorithms.
ui.Use a test password, not your real accou: Use a test password, not your real account password
ui.Argon2id requires: python3 -m pip instal: Argon2id requires: python3 -m pip install argon2-cffi. Keep the salt with the hash; it is not a secret.
ui.Generate random material using Python's: Generate random material using Python's cryptographically secure random source.
ui.Inspect a Python .pyc file and display i: Inspect a Python .pyc file and display its bytecode instructions. This is a lightweight disassembler, not a full source-code recovery tool.
ui.Python bytecode is version-specific. Use: Python bytecode is version-specific. Use the same Python major/minor version that created the .pyc file. The tool shows disassembled instructions and metadata; it does not execute the file or guarantee reconstruction of original source.
ui.• Fixed hashing: MD5, SHA-1, SHA3-256 an:
• Fixed hashing: MD5, SHA-1, SHA3-256 and SHA3-512 no longer fail.
• Translations moved to separate JSON files; Chinese and Spanish added.
• Dialogs, hints and error messages now follow the selected language.
ui.• Key panel with live validation and com:
• Key panel with live validation and compatible key generation.
• Fixed AES-256-GCM, Fernet, XOR and Atbash handling.
• Larger Enigma settings; Inter font with Noto Sans fallback.

messages.key.empty: The key is empty. Enter a key or press “Generate key”.
messages.key.aes.length: AES-256-GCM needs a HEX key of exactly 64 characters (32 bytes). Yours has {n}.
messages.key.aes.is_base64: This looks like a Base64 key (the Fernet format). AES-256-GCM needs HEX. Press “Convert key format”.
messages.key.aes.chars: An AES-256-GCM key may contain only 0–9 and a–f. Invalid character: “{ch}”.
messages.key.fernet.is_hex: This looks like a HEX key (the AES-256-GCM format). Fernet needs Base64. Press “Convert key format”.
messages.key.fernet.chars: A Fernet key must be Base64. Invalid character: “{ch}”.
messages.key.fernet.b64: This is not valid Base64. A Fernet key is 44 characters long and usually ends with “=”.
messages.key.fernet.length: A Fernet key must decode to exactly 32 bytes; yours decodes to {n}. Paste the whole key or generate a new one.
messages.key.vig.chars: A Vigenère key may contain only Latin letters A–Z. Invalid character: “{ch}”.
messages.token.bad_b64: The input is not a valid Base64 token. Paste the whole token produced by encryption, without extra characters.
messages.token.too_short: The token is too short for an AES-256-GCM message; it may be cut off.
messages.token.looks_fernet: This looks like a Fernet token (it starts with “gAAAA”). Select Fernet instead of AES-256-GCM.
messages.token.not_fernet: This does not look like a Fernet token (they start with “gAAAA”). If it was made with AES-256-GCM, select that algorithm.
messages.decrypt.failed: Decryption failed: the key is wrong, or the data was changed or damaged.
messages.decrypt.xor_failed: Decryption produced unreadable text. Most likely the key is wrong.
messages.decrypt.not_text: The data was decrypted, but it is not valid UTF-8 text.
messages.dep.missing: The “cryptography” package is required. Install it with: python3 -m pip install cryptography
messages.enigma.rotors: Choose three different rotors from I, II, III, IV, V.
messages.enigma.positions: Start positions and ring settings must be three letters A–Z, e.g. AAA.
messages.enigma.reflector: The reflector must be B or C.
messages.enigma.plug_format: Enter plugboard pairs like this: AB CD EF.
messages.enigma.plug_dupe: A letter can be used in only one plugboard pair.
messages.hint.vig: Vigenère key: Latin letters A–Z only.
messages.hint.caesar: Caesar uses the shift setting above. “Generate key” picks a random shift.
messages.hint.enigma: Enigma uses the rotor, position, ring and plugboard settings above. “Generate key” randomizes them.
messages.hint.none: This algorithm does not use a key.
messages.status.generated: ✓ A new {algo} key was generated. Save it: you need it to decrypt.
messages.status.enigma_random: ✓ Random Enigma settings applied. Note them down to decrypt later.
messages.argon2.missing: Install Argon2 support with: python3 -m pip install argon2-cffi
messages.hash.unsupported: This Python/OpenSSL build does not support {algo} (for example, FIPS mode blocks it). Choose another algorithm.
messages.bytecode.too_short: File is too short to be a standard modern .pyc file.
messages.bytecode.not_code: The file does not contain a recognized Python code object.
messages.bytecode.hint: Make sure the .pyc file was created by a compatible Python version.
